title: High Country Rapid Response & Resilience Fund
summary: Fast grants of up to $10,000 for nonprofits, tribal programs, and public agencies responding to wildfire, flooding, severe winter storms, and other emergencies in northern Arizona.
description: The High Country Rapid Response & Resilience Fund was created after the 2010 Schultz Fire and post-fire flooding outside Flagstaff. It provides fast, flexible funding to organizations helping residents during and after emergencies, and supports preparedness projects between disasters.

Requests are reviewed on a rolling basis, and most decisions are made within ten business days. During a declared emergency the Foundation may open a dedicated response window with expedited review, announced on this page.
impact_areas: Emergency food, water, shelter, and supplies
Community preparedness, evacuation planning, and resilience projects
Mental health and wellness support after disasters
populations_served: Households affected by wildfire, flooding, or severe weather
Older adults and people with disabilities during emergencies
Rural and tribal communities with limited emergency services

geography.summary: Organizations must be responding to emergencies affecting residents of Coconino, Yavapai, Navajo, or Apache counties, including tribal lands within those counties.

eligibility: Tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3), a public agency, a federally recognized tribe, tribal chapter, or tribal program, or a project with a qualified fiscal sponsor
Responding to a specific emergency, or carrying out a preparedness project, in the four-county region
Able to spend grant funds within six months of award
not_eligible: Direct payments to individuals (the Foundation funds organizations that assist individuals)
Costs already covered by insurance or FEMA reimbursement

funding.type: Emergency response or preparedness project support
funding.summary: Up to $10,000; most awards range from $2,500 to $7,500
funding.term: Funds must be spent within six months of award

dates.rolling: Requests are accepted year-round and reviewed on a rolling basis. Most decisions are made within ten business days.

how_to_apply.intro: The rapid response request is a two-page form designed to be completed in under an hour.

steps.title: Call or email first
steps.text: Contact the Vice President of Grants & Community Impact to describe the need. Staff will confirm whether the request fits the fund.

steps.title: Complete the request form
steps.text: Download and complete the Rapid Response Request Form. A budget table is included in the form.

steps.title: Submit by email
steps.text: Email the completed form to grants@cinderpeakscf.org with the subject line "Rapid Response – [Organization Name]".

steps.title: Decision and payment
steps.text: Most decisions are made within ten business days. Approved grants are paid by direct deposit or check.

review_criteria: Urgency and severity of the need
The applicant's connection to the affected community
Coordination with emergency management, tribal, and relief agencies

reporting.summary: Grantees submit a one-page Rapid Response Use of Funds Report within 60 days of spending the grant.
items: How funds were used and how many people were helped
Photos, if available, with permission noted
Any remaining needs in the community
reporting.due: Within 60 days after funds are spent
